records.subject: Electrode separation
records.conditions: Platinum-electrode ferricyanide/ferrocyanide cell; cold-above-hot configuration; separations up to 150 cm; electrode temperatures 293.1 and 313.1 K.
records.quote: The effect of electrode separation on the power conversion efficiency of a ferricyanide/ferrocyanide thermogalvanic cell containing platinum electrodes was studied at electrode separations up to 150 cm, using the ''cold-above-hot'' electrode configuration.
context_quotes: The open-circuit potential difference is almost independent of electrode separation, but the short-circuit current density falls continuously with increasing electrode separation, while the power conversion efficiency increases asymptotically to a plateau value of ca. 0.04% at a separation near 150 cm.
This corresponds to an efficiency of ca. 0.6% relative to that of a Carnot engine operating between the temperatures of 293.1 and 313.1 K used in the present study.
